scope: Finite deterministic GMI at the declared interface: ecology (E, budgets, horizon), obligation Omega, machine (S,I,O,delta,F,alpha,c), development law D. Admissibility only (DU-1); no claim that neutral search reaches any capability.

rows.inputs: raw sensor stream X_t with declared sensor type, noise model, bandwidth and latency contract
rows.allowed_info: current semantic cut c(X_t) and calibration context; no privileged future or oracle side channel
rows.required_behaviour: emit response r_t that distinguishes obligation-relevant equivalence classes of X_t under declared noise
rows.success_metric: exact 0/1 correctness on the obligation partition, or L2/0-1 error within declared tolerance epsilon
rows.resource_metric: sensor bandwidth, encoding bits |c|, and transformation cost tau for the perception map
rows.negative_twin: single-state ecology where X_t is already obligation-sufficient and sensor-independent: perception adds cost with no accuracy gain
rows.strongest_parent: signal detection theory (Green & Swets); psychophysics of sensory thresholds
rows.atlas_reduction: sensing / perception — environment->machine semantic cut (GG53); sensing capacity matters only for obligation-relevant distinctions
rows.falsifier: a perceiver succeeding without distinguishing two X values the obligation separates, or an adequate protocol using fewer sensor bits than kappa(H) on the registered cut

rows.inputs: multi-source stream (x0,x1,context q) with finite access constraint (only one source exposed per step)
rows.allowed_info: context-conditioned routing decision plus the selected source; no simultaneous full product
rows.required_behaviour: route the obligation-relevant source for the current context q (achieve context-dependent accuracy above every fixed route)
rows.success_metric: exact accuracy on x_q obligation: 8/8 routed vs 6/8 best fixed source (GG55 census)
rows.resource_metric: routing decision cost c_r plus accessed source width versus exposure cost c_e(|U|-E|E_x|)
rows.negative_twin: single-source or context-independent ecology where fixed routing already achieves the routed accuracy: attentional routing wastes c_r with no gain
rows.strongest_parent: attention / routing literature (Posner; Bundesen TVA); GG55 conditional routing advantage
rows.atlas_reduction: attention — content-conditioned allocation of finite internal cut access (GG55)
rows.falsifier: a fixed source achieving 8/8 on the registered (x0,x1,q)->x_q ecology, or a routing policy claimed beneficial while violating c_r + lambda p_r < c_e(|U|-E|E_x|)

rows.inputs: transient cue that must be retained across a short interference-filled delay before response
rows.allowed_info: bounded persistent state S_working carried through the delay; no external store access during delay
rows.required_behaviour: maintain the cue distinction through the delay and emit it correctly at probe time despite interference
rows.success_metric: exact reproduction accuracy after delay, or within-tolerance recall; must degrade monotonically with load and interference
rows.resource_metric: persistent state cardinality |S_working|, maintenance transformation cost, and interference susceptibility
rows.negative_twin: zero-delay or cue-redundant ecology where the response is computable from immediate input: working memory adds state cost with no benefit
rows.strongest_parent: Baddeley working-memory model; Cowan capacity limits; GG54 temporal cut theory
rows.atlas_reduction: memory / working memory — temporal semantic cut from past process to future process (GG54)
rows.falsifier: exact delayed reproduction of m alternatives with fewer than m distinguishable persistent states (violates |S_memory| >= m)

rows.inputs: autobiographical event (what, where, when, context) presented once with spatiotemporal tags
rows.allowed_info: episodic store plus cue-driven retrieval channel; no semantic summary alone suffices for the probe
rows.required_behaviour: reinstate the specific bound episode from a partial cue, distinguishing it from similar episodes
rows.success_metric: cued recall precision and source discrimination (hit rate vs false reinstatement) on the obligation partition
rows.resource_metric: episodic entry count N_t, encoding/retrieval cost, and consolidation cost to long-term store
rows.negative_twin: fully predictable or stateless-recomputable ecology where each query is answered from a generative rule: episodic storage wastes capacity with no accuracy gain
rows.strongest_parent: Tulving episodic/semantic distinction; Clayton & Dickinson what-where-when paradigm
rows.atlas_reduction: memory — temporal cut plus distinguishing episode identity beyond semantic summary (GG57 multi-time cut)
rows.falsifier: a memoryless policy matching episodic cued recall on episodes the registered ecology makes episodically distinct without the |S| >= N_t bound

rows.inputs: repeated encounters with category members carrying stable statistical regularities across episodes
rows.allowed_info: compressed semantic store abstracting away episode identity; no verbatim trace of each encounter retained
rows.required_behaviour: answer category-level probes (generalisation, property inference) by de-duplicating shared structure across episodes
rows.success_metric: generalisation accuracy to held-out members and false-memory resistance on the semantic quotient
rows.resource_metric: semantic code size, abstraction cost, and retrieval transformation tau
rows.negative_twin: one-shot unique-episode ecology where every probe asks for a specific past token: semantic compression loses distinctions and lowers accuracy
rows.strongest_parent: Collins & Quillian semantic networks; Rogers & McClelland semantic cognition; category learning theory
rows.atlas_reduction: compression / semantic encoding — reduced carrier under exact or approximate response constraints (GG59 atlas row)
rows.falsifier: a semantic summary merging two obligation-distinct states while still claimed exact on the registered quotient

rows.inputs: repeated practice on a sensorimotor or cognitive skill under a stable transformation requirement
rows.allowed_info: compiled procedural routine (production/circuit/policy) retrieved without declarative recall of instruction traces
rows.required_behaviour: execute the skill faster and with lower online transformation cost after compilation, with retained accuracy
rows.success_metric: execution latency and online tau reduction at matched accuracy; interference/transfer cost to other skills
rows.resource_metric: compiled code size, compilation (search) cost, and online execution cost
rows.negative_twin: single-trial novel-task ecology where each problem requires declarative reasoning from scratch: procedural compilation never amortizes its cost
rows.strongest_parent: Anderson ACT-R proceduralisation; Fitts & Posner skill acquisition; production-system compilation
rows.atlas_reduction: skill compilation — retained sub-quotient at PVR-3 reuse threshold; same accounting as hierarchy chunking
rows.falsifier: a compiled routine claimed faster while requiring the same online declarative search steps as the uncompiled trace (PVR-3 threshold miscount, re-run the checker)

rows.inputs: probe cue plus external/persistent store with residual obligation-relevant distinctions
rows.allowed_info: retrieval transformation over the store plus current cue; store coverage and reliability declared
rows.required_behaviour: return the obligation-relevant residual that the parametric state alone lacks, within the retrieval cut capacity
rows.success_metric: residual accuracy gain over no-retrieval baseline at matched store coverage; retrieval precision/recall
rows.resource_metric: index size, retrieval query cost tau_retrieve, and communication cut width
rows.negative_twin: ecology where the store carries no residual beyond the parametric state or is unreliable: retrieval adds cost with zero or negative net accuracy
rows.strongest_parent: information retrieval (Salton); RAG literature; GG12 task-directed acquisition — retrieval is external cut allocation
rows.atlas_reduction: retrieval / RAG — external persistent side-information channel + retrieval transformation (GG59 atlas row)
rows.falsifier: retrieval helping beyond its declared residual or reliability contract, or a stored fact retrieved without being in the store (information creation from nothing)

rows.inputs: episodic traces accumulated over episodes plus a stable long-term store with replay opportunity
rows.allowed_info: offline replay channel and consolidation transformation that restructures traces into semantic/procedural form
rows.required_behaviour: integrate traces so later retrieval needs fewer active states (saving t - ceil(log2 N_t)) while preserving joint retention
rows.success_metric: retention accuracy after consolidation at reduced active-state budget; CSR-1 minimum M*_t = N_t preserved
rows.resource_metric: replay steps, consolidation transformation cost, and resulting long-term code size
rows.negative_twin: ecology with no recurrence and infinite active memory: consolidation's restructuring yields no saving because every trace is probed only once and never interferes
rows.strongest_parent: McClelland et al. complementary learning systems; CSR-1 consolidation theorem (GMI)
rows.atlas_reduction: consolidation — offline restructuring that preserves multi-time temporal cut width while reducing active-state load (GG57/CSR-1)
rows.falsifier: exact retention of N_t joint histories with fewer than N_t joint states and no side channel (violates GG57)

rows.inputs: accumulated distinctions that outgrow the state budget or become obligation-irrelevant under drift
rows.allowed_info: policy choosing which distinctions to merge/drop; no unbounded state expansion allowed
rows.required_behaviour: drop exactly those distinctions whose loss costs least future obligation error, respecting the forgetting threshold
rows.success_metric: future expected loss after forgetting versus random or no-forgetting baseline at matched budget
rows.resource_metric: retained state cardinality after forgetting and relearning cost for dropped distinctions if they recur
rows.negative_twin: unbounded-state or fully obligation-relevant ecology where every past distinction will be probed: forgetting strictly increases expected error
rows.strongest_parent: Hardt et al. forgetting theory; continual learning catastrophic forgetting literature; CSR-1 forgetting condition
rows.atlas_reduction: memory — catastrophic forgetting as developmental transition merging states required by retained obligations (GG57 / CSR-1)
rows.falsifier: forgetting a distinction the registered future probe set still requires while claiming no accuracy loss on that probe

rows.inputs: temporal stream with predictable suffix given a learned world model and current state estimate
rows.allowed_info: predictive response representation (world model) plus current belief state; no oracle future observation
rows.required_behaviour: emit the predictive response that minimises obligation-relevant surprise (next observation or latent consequence)
rows.success_metric: next-step predictive accuracy and calibration of forecast uncertainty on the registered stream
rows.resource_metric: model code size, inference tau, and belief-state maintenance cost
rows.negative_twin: i.i.d. unpredictable stream where history carries zero mutual information about the next sample: prediction adds compute with chance accuracy
rows.strongest_parent: predictive coding (Rao & Ballard); Friston; world-model literature (Ha & Schmidhuber)
rows.atlas_reduction: world model — predictive response representation used by control/planning (GG59 atlas row)
rows.falsifier: a predictor beating the declared Bayes risk on the registered stream without additional history or side information

rows.inputs: instance stream where some distinctions are reusable across future obligations and others are idiosyncratic
rows.allowed_info: naming/boundary decision that groups instances into a class when PVR-3 reuse threshold is crossed
rows.required_behaviour: form a new concept (name + boundary) exactly when reuse amortises naming cost; place boundaries at the bang-bang optimum
rows.success_metric: reuse-weighted accuracy: concept-assisted future probe accuracy minus naming cost, versus no-concept baseline
rows.resource_metric: number of concepts retained, boundary description bits, and retrieval cost per use
rows.negative_twin: ecology where no distinction recurs (one-off instances): every concept pays naming cost with zero future reuse
rows.strongest_parent: Murphy concepts and categories; GMI concept formation trigger + granularity theorems (bang-bang)
rows.atlas_reduction: hierarchy / abstraction — semantic quotient at PVR-3 threshold (GG59 atlas row)
rows.falsifier: a concept whose PVR-3 break-even is not crossed yet claimed beneficial, or a boundary not at the registered bang-bang optimum while claimed optimal

rows.inputs: structured query whose meaning is a product of primitive meanings (e.g. a* -> b* with constraints)
rows.allowed_info: compositional code where each primitive's code is reused; no holistic codebook larger than the product
rows.required_behaviour: compose primitive answers into the correct product response without enumerating the full product table
rows.success_metric: accuracy on held-out compositions (systematic generalisation) and description-length saving versus holistic enumeration
rows.resource_metric: codebook size (|primitives| not |product|) and composition transformation cost
rows.negative_twin: ecology with no product structure (idiosyncratic mapping per compound): compositional codes pay decomposition overhead with no generalisation gain
rows.strongest_parent: Fodor & Pylyshyn compositionality; SCAN systematicity (Lake & Baroni); formal language theory
rows.atlas_reduction: composition / language morphology — product meaning space with recombination witnesses (GG27/GAC-5)
rows.falsifier: a holistic code beating the compositional bound inside the registered product regime at matched resource budget

rows.inputs: action sequence where a contiguous subsequence recurs across tasks with shared dynamics
rows.allowed_info: skill library of retained sub-quotients; option/macro that compiles the subsequence into one decision
rows.required_behaviour: chunk the recurring subsequence into a skill when PVR-3 threshold is crossed; second-level chunking self-limits as C lowers
rows.success_metric: planning and execution cost reduction across tasks versus flat search; skill reuse count and transfer
rows.resource_metric: skill description size, skill retrieval cost, and retained state per level
rows.negative_twin: ecology where no subsequence recurs (each sequence is unique): chunking pays retention cost with zero cross-task reuse
rows.strongest_parent: Sutton options framework; Newell & Rosenbloom chunking; GMI hierarchical chunking theorem
rows.atlas_reduction: hierarchy — skill is retained sub-quotient; levels self-limit because retaining a level raises the next bar (GG59 atlas row)
rows.falsifier: a second hierarchical level claimed beneficial while its PVR-3 reuse threshold is not crossed (measured 10-20% of first level, 0% at high storage/low recurrence)

rows.inputs: current state, action set, transition model, and goal predicate over future states (plus horizon/budget)
rows.allowed_info: internal simulation (model-based lookahead) consuming tau; no oracle rollout beyond the declared model fidelity
rows.required_behaviour: return a trajectory whose next action is optimal under the model and stop expanding when no expansion changes the action or pays (EVC <= 0)
rows.success_metric: goal attainment rate and action optimality under the model; planning-depth vs accuracy tradeoff
rows.resource_metric: simulation steps tau, search frontier size, and model-query cost
rows.negative_twin: myopic or model-free-sufficient ecology where the optimal action is computable from immediate reward: planning adds tau with no action change
rows.strongest_parent: classical planning (Ghallab et al.); model-based RL (Sutton & Barto); planning semantic resolution (GMI)
rows.atlas_reduction: planning — transformation process over future-contingency semantic state; difficulty in tau and conflict structure (GG59)
rows.falsifier: a plan claimed adequate at a resolution the semantic resolution ladder says is insufficient, or an expansion with EVC > 0 left unexpanded while claimed optimal

rows.inputs: uncertain world/task distribution with probes whose answers have declared cost and downstream value
rows.allowed_info: probe proposal plus Bayesian or worst-case uncertainty measure over the obligation-relevant quotient
rows.required_behaviour: select the probe whose expected reduction in obligation-relevant uncertainty minus resources is maximal (non-negative to act)
rows.success_metric: information gain per cost and downstream decision accuracy versus no-probe or random-probe baseline
rows.resource_metric: probe execution cost, search/experiment budget, and time to decision
rows.negative_twin: fully known or value-free ecology where every probe's downstream decision is already determined: exploration adds cost with zero obligation-relevant gain
rows.strongest_parent: Thompson sampling / bandits; optimal experiment design (Lindley); Blackwell value of information
rows.atlas_reduction: exploration / causal discovery — action chosen partly for downstream semantic/developmental state change (GG59)
rows.falsifier: a probe whose measured obligation-relevant uncertainty reduction contradicts the booked value net of cost, or curiosity-driven probing with negative net value claimed beneficial

rows.inputs: observational distribution P(X,Y) plus admissible intervention set and declared graph class
rows.allowed_info: causal identification machinery (back-door, do-calculus) and supported intervention evaluation; no privileged counterfactual labels
rows.required_behaviour: distinguish P(Y|X) from P(Y|do(X)) and report identifiability correctly within the declared graph scope
rows.success_metric: identification correctness on the registered SCM (CAU-5a tables) and sign/bound accuracy where identifiable
rows.resource_metric: graph search cost and identification proof length
rows.negative_twin: ecology where the target is purely associational and no decision conditions on an intervention: causal machinery adds cost with no decision difference
rows.strongest_parent: Pearl causality (do-calculus); Spirtes et al.; CAU-1..5 theorems (GMI)
rows.atlas_reduction: causal semantic information — admitted interventions + constitution (GG29); CAU-5a no-universal-sign separator
rows.falsifier: a fixed learner separating W1's worlds from the identical stream, or a supported adjustment disagreeing with surgical evaluation on W4a/W4b (re-run test_causal_rungs_v1.py)

rows.inputs: observed outcome under an actual intervention plus the structural model and response table
rows.allowed_info: counterfactual computation (twin network / abduction-action-prediction) within the declared response-table scope
rows.required_behaviour: compute P(Y_x' | x, y) or PN correctly where rung-3 is identifiable and abstain where only bounds exist
rows.success_metric: counterfactual probability correctness on W5A/W5B (PN 1/2 vs 1) and bound soundness where not point-identified
rows.resource_metric: counterfactual inference cost and model specification burden
rows.negative_twin: ecology where no decision conditions on a contrary-to-fact branch (only factual or interventional queries): counterfactual reasoning adds cost with no decision value
rows.strongest_parent: Lewis counterfactuals; Pearl rung-3 theory; Balke-Pearl bounds; CAU-5c (GMI)
rows.atlas_reduction: rung-3 counterfactuals — response-table semantics under uniform root law (CAU-5c)
rows.falsifier: PN claimed point-identified where Balke-Pearl says only bounds exist, or miscount in W5A/W5B rung laws or PN values (re-run test_causal_rungs_v1.py)

rows.inputs: internal decision state: surviving candidate set S, adequate-action sets Gamma(w), pending probes and costs
rows.allowed_info: derived confidence conf=|adequate|/|S|, error likelihood 1-conf, and expected value of cognition EVC
rows.required_behaviour: gate action with confidence=1 iff C(S) nonempty, continue probing iff EVC>0, and select among reasoning strategies by worst-case total value
rows.success_metric: calibration (adequacy rate at each conf level equals that level) and decision accuracy per cost
rows.resource_metric: metacognitive computation (EVC evaluation) and strategy-register evaluation cost
rows.negative_twin: ecology where C(S) is always a singleton (always know what to do) and probing is free: metacognition adds monitoring cost with no decision change
rows.strongest_parent: Nelson & Narens metacognition; Fleming & Lau confidence; META-1..4 theorems (GMI) — confidence as surviving-candidate margin
rows.atlas_reduction: metacognition — confidence / error likelihood / EVC as derived internal objects of the acquisition value function (META-1..4)
rows.falsifier: a candidate subset where max-confidence action does not minimise EC, or where max-EVC test does not match the TDA-1 minimiser where the 13/35 greedy condition says it must (re-run test_metacognition_v1.py)

rows.inputs: observations of another agent's actions plus declared ecology of that agent's incentives and information
rows.allowed_info: agent model as retained state predicting the other's policy (copycat/contrarian/beauty-contest) plus belief hierarchy of bounded depth
rows.required_behaviour: predict and best-respond to the other's policy where opponent-type matters; recurse to the exact closure depth (e.g. beauty ladder depth 3)
rows.success_metric: joint payoff versus fixed-policy baseline; opponent-type prediction accuracy; recursion depth correctness
rows.resource_metric: agent-model state size, inference tau, and recursion depth cost
rows.negative_twin: ecology with fixed non-strategic partners or uninformative opponents: opponent modelling loses exactly its price with no payoff gain (TOM-1 negative twin)
rows.strongest_parent: Premack & Woodruff theory of mind; Stahl level-k; Camerer Ho Chong cognitive hierarchy; TOM-1..3 (GMI)
rows.atlas_reduction: multi-agent / ToM — opponent models as retained state paying for itself only at intermediate uncertainty (TOM-1)
rows.falsifier: a fixed policy scoring 2 against both copycat and contrarian (violates TOM-1 forcing), or beauty_ladder() != [5,3,2,1,1,1] (re-run test_strategic_tom_v1.py)

rows.inputs: shared obligation and context plus a declared message channel with width/cost/noise contract
rows.allowed_info: protocol over the shared semantic cut; messages conditioned on local observations and common ground
rows.required_behaviour: implement the distributed semantic cut: send exactly the distinctions the joint obligation requires, no more and no fewer
rows.success_metric: distributed task success rate at matched message width; information-theoretic efficiency (bits per required distinction)
rows.resource_metric: message width (symbols), channel uses, and protocol description cost
rows.negative_twin: single-agent or fully shared-observation ecology where the receiver already sees the sender's information: communication adds channel cost with zero joint gain
rows.strongest_parent: Shannon communication theory; Lewis signalling games; SC-1 semantic cut theorem (GMI)
rows.atlas_reduction: language / communication — protocol implementing distributed semantic cuts; required distinctions derive from shared obligation (SC-1/GG25)
rows.falsifier: a distributed protocol using fewer symbols than chi(H) on a registered interface (beats the semantic cut bound)

rows.inputs: demonstration trajectory of an expert (state-action sequence) under a declared embodiment mapping
rows.allowed_info: observation of expert behaviour plus a correspondence mapping between demonstrator and imitator action spaces
rows.required_behaviour: reproduce the expert's policy (not just trajectory) in the imitator's embodiment, generalising beyond the demo states
rows.success_metric: policy fidelity on held-out states and task success after imitation versus from-scratch learning
rows.resource_metric: demonstration count, correspondence search cost, and imitation learning compute
rows.negative_twin: ecology where the demonstrator's policy is already known or the embodiment mapping is identity-trivial: copying adds no information beyond the known policy
rows.strongest_parent: Bandura social learning; Schaal imitation learning; Byrne & Russon programme-level imitation
rows.atlas_reduction: social learning — learning law operating on expert trajectories as input ecology (developmental lift T1)
rows.falsifier: an imitator claimed to match the expert policy while failing on a state the expert visits with a different obligated action that the mapping should preserve

rows.inputs: learner state estimate plus a teachable procedure whose learning curve and transfer are declared
rows.allowed_info: pedagogical actions (demonstration, instruction, scaffolding, feedback) selected to maximise learner's future obligation success
rows.required_behaviour: choose teaching interventions that minimise learner's time-to-mastery at matched teaching cost; respect n > 1 + S/(C-U) break-even
rows.success_metric: learner sample efficiency and post-teaching transfer accuracy versus no-teaching or random-teaching baseline
rows.resource_metric: teaching actions/instructions sent and teacher planning cost
rows.negative_twin: ecology where the learner already knows the task or learns faster alone (teaching overhead exceeds solo cost): teaching adds latency with no learner gain
rows.strongest_parent: Thornton & Knudsen teaching theory; Csibra & Gergely natural pedagogy; GMI teaching/culture break-even
rows.atlas_reduction: teaching — pedagogical lift where teacher's obligation is learner's future capability (recursive morphogenesis lift)
rows.falsifier: a teaching run claimed beneficial while violating n > 1 + S/(C-U) break-even at the registered S/C/U and population fidelity (check the arithmetic)

rows.inputs: population of learners plus a transmission channel with fidelity contract and generational turnover
rows.allowed_info: cultural store (artifacts, language, institutions) transmitted with declared fidelity; no unbounded individual memory assumed
rows.required_behaviour: ratchet complexity across generations so the population's frontier exceeds any single lifetime's reachable set
rows.success_metric: generational increase in task complexity solved and retention of prior gains (no cultural loss)
rows.resource_metric: population size, transmission fidelity overhead, and cultural store size
rows.negative_twin: ecology with fully faithful individual learning and no generational turnover (immortal perfect learners): culture adds transmission cost with no frontier expansion
rows.strongest_parent: Tomasello cultural ratchet; Boyd & Richerson dual inheritance; Henrich cumulative culture theory
rows.atlas_reduction: evolution / culture — population-level developmental process with declared viability and transmission obligation (GG59)
rows.falsifier: a population claimed to ratchet while some generation's transmission fidelity is below the registered threshold yet no loss occurs (violates the fidelity contract)

rows.inputs: own internal state and process traces plus a probe family over self-state
rows.allowed_info: self-observation channel (interoception / execution trace) and a self-model representation with declared fidelity
rows.required_behaviour: maintain a self-model that correctly predicts own future responses and resource needs within the probe family
rows.success_metric: self-prediction accuracy and resource-estimation calibration on the declared self-probe set
rows.resource_metric: self-monitoring cost, self-model state size, and update frequency
rows.negative_twin: ecology where the system's behaviour is fully determined by a fixed known policy with no hidden state: self-modelling adds monitoring cost with no prediction gain
rows.strongest_parent: Metzinger self-model theory; Rochat self-awareness; GMI self-probe / reflective quotient
rows.atlas_reduction: self-probe / reflection — self-probe family and diagonal boundary (GR1-GR2)
rows.falsifier: an exact self-prediction succeeding under an admitted inverting intervention within the declared self-probe family (violates GR diagonal impossibility)

rows.inputs: own performance history plus a declared improvement operator (self-rewrite, hyperparameter update, architecture edit)
rows.allowed_info: introspective evaluation and a governed self-modification channel with verification gate
rows.required_behaviour: apply self-modifications that improve the capability frontier or resource efficiency and pass the verification gate
rows.success_metric: frontier expansion or resource reduction after self-modification versus no-modification baseline at matched verification
rows.resource_metric: self-modification search cost, verification cost, and risk of regression
rows.negative_twin: ecology where the system is already at the global optimum or self-modification is unverifiable: self-improvement adds search and verification cost with no frontier gain
rows.strongest_parent: Schmidhuber Godel machine; self-modifying code literature; GMI recursive morphogenesis lift
rows.atlas_reduction: recursive morphogenesis / self-modification — state includes own update description (T2 lift)
rows.falsifier: a self-modification claimed beneficial while the verification gate fails or the frontier does not expand under the declared ecology and resource contract

rows.inputs: task requiring an external transformation (calculator, code executor, database, actuator) with declared tool contract
rows.allowed_info: tool-call channel plus tool inputs/outputs; internal state alone does not contain the tool's information or transformation
rows.required_behaviour: compose with the tool so joint system achieves the obligation while internal tau is reduced by the tool's contribution
rows.success_metric: task success rate with tool versus without, at matched tool-call budget and communication cost

rows.atlas_reduction: tool / oracle use — composition with external process plus tool-call cut; moves tau across boundary (GG58)

rows.inputs: population of agents with overlapping or coupled obligations and a declared social topology and communication contract

rows.strongest_parent: Olson collective action; Malone & Bernstein collective intelligence; GG25 team centralization (GMI)
rows.atlas_reduction: multi-agent intelligence — composed process network with internal semantic cuts; GG25 product tensorization
